messages.subject: Re: Manual calibration
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lijuan Wang and Tam Nguyen, I've done a manual calibration of my SWAT model in R-SWAT and got NSE 0.20 and R2 0.28. I need to increase the efficiency of the model with appreciable performance indices values. How shall we proceed? What are all the parameters and their range that can be considered to have optimality in the solution at the end. Pls let me know and your support is highly appreciated and is more necessary as I'm doing this for the past few weeks (3-4 weeks). It's my humble request. I also provide the optimization/uncertainty plot too... I require your guidance in understanding the hydrograph obtained too..... Pls... Pls... Pls....

On Fri, Jun 30, 2023 at 8:11 PM Lijuan Wang <lijua...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi  Tam,
> Thank you very much for your reply and my last problem has been solved.
> However, I have encountered a new problem. My calibration result is very bad (Daily flow from 2000-2020). Lower NSE, KGE and R2.
> What should I do to improve the performance, do you have any suggestions?
>
> Thank you very much.
>
> 在2023年6月27日星期二 UTC+8 17:53:05<Tam Nguyen> 写道：
> > Hi, parameter is the value from the left panel (as shown from your attached figure), simulated results are in the working folder - just look for "TxtInOut_1" folder
> >
> > On Tuesday, June 27, 2023 at 8:40:32 AM UTC+2 lijua...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > Hi Tam,
> > > I ran RSWAT  in the manual calibration, and I got good NSE, R2 and KGE.
> > > But, how could I get the input parameter value for this good result and how could I get the simulated values?
> > > Thank you!
>

messages.subject: Re: Manual calibration
messages.body_plain:
might be this paper could give you some hints

https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4441/10/1/6

I just want to add that - first detect if there is some processes in your basin that the model does not accounted for (e.g., reservoir, water conversion, irrigation, etc..) or if there is some problem with the input data (e.g., rainfall) and observed streamflow. Then you can see which is the most sensitive parameters - take these parameters and try to vary them in a wide (plausible) range.

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone. I am a user who is using R-SWAT (ArcSWAT) without the GUI version. I am trying to simulate water quality using R-SWAT, and I have encountered a question during the process of adjusting parameters through swatParam.txt. Currently, swatParam.txt does not contain parameters related to .swq. As most of you may know, the parameters included in .swq are necessary for routing water quality in streams (based on qual2E). Therefore, I have limitations in optimizing parameters and performing sensitivity evaluations by adjusting the .swq-related parameters. I would greatly appreciate it if anyone could suggest a solution or provide guidance on this matter.
Thanks.
